# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 46 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 46 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_046_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 12, Part 3 — How the Angel of Righteousness Helps

**46:1** "I asked him, lord, now that I have come to the end of these commandments, whether I should be able to keep them, since they are so great and serious." "You shall keep them," he said, "if your heart is pure toward God. And all who have cleansed their hearts from the empty desires of this age shall keep them and shall live to God."

**46:2** "Lord," I said, "now that I have heard these commandments, if any man has no power to keep them because of the weakness of his flesh, what shall he do?" "If he undertakes them and does not keep them, and if his heart is turned away from the Lord, he shall live in death. But he who undertakes them from his whole heart and strives to do what is right, but stumbles from time to time on account of the weakness of his flesh — this man lives, because the Lord is compassionate."

**46:3** "The Lord sees his heart that it is pure and he has compassion on this man and forgives him all his wanderings. He strengthens the man and gives him to keep the commandments of the Angel of Righteousness, and grants him salvation."

**46:4** "But to the man who lives in forgetfulness and has not kept the commandments of the Lord, the Lord delivers him to the angel of punishment. This angel torments that man for his wickedness, and he is chastised unto salvation."

**46:5** "But Lord," I said, "how can the Lord be both so gentle and also allow such chastisement?" "Listen," he said. "The Lord is compassionate in all his deeds and in all his words. He has love of humanity and gentleness and long-suffering and mercy. Therefore, as long as a man repents he has hope. But when he turns away from God and sins repeatedly without repentance, there is no hope for him."

---

*EMET renders the Greek of P.Mich. 130 with maximal literalness, preserving the twofold Angel of Righteousness / Angel of Punishment framework.*
